# WebRiskAudit

> WebRiskAudit is an open-source, non-commercial passive security scanner. Given a domain, it runs a small set of automated checks against publicly visible signals and reports each result (pass, warning, fail, inconclusive or info) with the evidence, fix and references it has, plus a score from 0 to 100 and a grade from A to F. Results are heuristic and are not a substitute for a professional security assessment.

- Website: https://webriskaudit.com
- Source code: https://github.com/portakalp/webriskaudit
- Author: Taha Gökalp Bakar (https://github.com/portakalp)
- Cost: free to use. Nothing is sold and there are no paid plans.

## What it checks

- Email authentication: the SPF record (qualifier of "all", DNS lookup count), the DMARC policy (including the policy inherited from a parent domain) and a DKIM key under common selectors.
- HTTPS and TLS: whether the certificate is trusted and not close to expiry, whether http:// redirects to https://, and the Strict-Transport-Security header.
- HTTP security headers on the home page: Content-Security-Policy (script sources), clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, cookie flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) and software versions in server headers.
- Informational, not scored: CDN or edge network, a privacy policy link on the home page, Permissions-Policy and deprecated headers such as X-XSS-Protection.

## How it works

- Only passive requests are made: DNS lookups (the domain's addresses and its SPF, DMARC and DKIM records), a TLS handshake on port 443 to read the certificate, and HTTP GET requests for the http:// and https:// home page, following up to 5 redirects; each HTTPS request makes its own TLS handshake.
- Nothing beyond these requests is made: no link crawling, port scanning, fuzzing, authentication or exploitation is attempted. Requests to non-public addresses are refused.
- The score counts only checks that reached a verdict: a pass earns a check's full weight, a warning half, a fail nothing. Inconclusive checks are left out, and if checks worth less than half of the points reach a verdict, no score is given.
- No account is needed. The domain is sent to the WebRiskAudit API, which runs the checks and returns the report. The API keeps no database of scans; it caches a report in memory for 10 minutes, and its log records each scanned domain with the outcome, score, grade and duration, but no IP addresses.

## Limitations

- Results are automated and heuristic. DKIM selectors cannot be listed, so a missing DKIM key is reported as inconclusive, and CDN detection relies on response headers.
- Only the home page is inspected; headers or cookies set on other pages are not seen.
- A high score does not mean a site is secure, and a low score does not mean it is compromised.
- It is not a penetration test, a vulnerability assessment or legal or compliance advice.
